around.headline: Police say an organised gang is behind a string of Ganesh idol thefts from roadside stalls
around.summary: After a Ganesh idol was stolen in broad daylight from a Bengaluru stall — the theft caught clearly on CCTV — police say a gang is now on their radar for targeting multiple stalls the same way, per The Hindu and NDTV. If you're running a festival-week stall, a basic camera on your stock and keeping high-value idols out of easy reach can make the difference.

around.headline: Two-wheeler ban on Airport Road and Electronics City flyovers put on hold, for now
around.summary: Traffic police have paused the proposed two-wheeler restriction on Bengaluru's Airport Road and Electronics City elevated corridors, per NDTV and The New Indian Express. Riders can keep using these routes, but treat this as a pause rather than a final call — the phase-in plan is still on the table.

around.headline: Metro Green Line hit by a technical glitch
around.summary: BMRCL confirmed a technical glitch disrupted Green Line services yesterday, per goodreturns.in. If you rely on this line, check today's live Namma Metro status before you head out in case intermittent issues carry over.

around.headline: South Bengaluru's mega ring road gets the green light on land acquisition
around.summary: The long-pending South Bengaluru ring road project has cleared land-acquisition approval, per Bangalore Mirror. If you own or rent property along the proposed corridor, it's worth checking whether your area falls in the acquisition zone before you make any long-term plans there.

around.headline: Food-safety crackdown continues: more expired goods seized, a restaurant shut for hygiene
around.summary: Karnataka's food safety department's raids on Bengaluru quick-commerce dark stores have now turned up over Rs 1.4 crore in expired and mislabelled food and medicine, and a separate restaurant was shut after an inspection flagged an unhygienic kitchen, per Indian Express and Deccan Herald. Worth a second look at expiry dates on your next quick-commerce medicine or packaged-food order.

around.headline: Brent crude crosses $100 a barrel as US-Iran tensions escalate
around.summary: Oil prices pushed past $100 a barrel after the US struck five Iranian oil tankers and Iran hit back at ten ships and a base in Jordan, per Al Jazeera. A sustained rise at this level typically feeds into pump prices and cab/auto fares within a few weeks, so budget your commute costs with that in mind.

street_smart.title: You're driving over a Bengaluru flyover in peak-hour traffic when a sports car right next to you starts doing donuts and hard revs, weaving within a few feet of your bonnet — like the viral Lamborghini flyover-stunt video from today. What's the smartest move?
street_smart.based_on: News18, Sept 9 — a video of a Lamborghini doing dangerous stunts on a Bengaluru flyover in peak traffic went viral, sparking fury over road safety. This bystander-reaction-to-a-reckless-stunt-driver mechanism is distinct from the wrong-side-vehicle, road-rage-chase and traffic-cop-assault scenarios used earlier this year, and hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: Other drivers around you are honking and a couple of two-wheeler riders have slowed to film the car on their phones while still moving alongside it.

choices.text: Keep a safe distance, don't engage with the car at all, and once you're stopped somewhere safe, note the number plate, time and location to report it — via 100 or the Bengaluru traffic police's complaint channel.
choices.feedback: Correct. A stunt driver weaving through peak traffic is unpredictable — the safest move is always distance first. Reporting with a plate number, time and location gives police something concrete to act on without you needing to intervene in person, or risk a collision trying to record while still moving.

choices.text: Speed up and try to get past the car quickly so you're out of its way.
choices.feedback: Risky. Overtaking a driver who is already swerving unpredictably at speed puts you directly in their path at the exact moment they're least in control. Slowing and creating distance is safer than a race to get clear.

choices.text: Roll down your window and shout at the driver to stop, or pull up alongside at the next signal to confront them.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Confronting a driver who's already behaving recklessly — and is possibly intoxicated or looking for attention — is exactly how ordinary traffic disputes turn into the road-rage assaults that keep showing up in Bengaluru's news. You gain nothing from a confrontation; you only add risk to yourself.

choices.text: Slow down to match the car's pace and film it closely on your phone so you have clear footage, even if it means driving one-handed for a bit.
choices.feedback: Risky. Filming while driving splits your attention exactly when you need it most, right next to a car that's already out of control. If you must record, do it stopped and from a safe distance — a shaky one-handed clip isn't worth the crash risk.

takeaways: Never confront or chase a reckless or stunt driver — pull back and create distance first, every time.
Report reckless driving to 100 (or the Bengaluru traffic police) with the vehicle number, time and location; you don't have to intervene in person for a complaint to count.
If you want to record evidence, do it from a stopped, safe position — never one-handed while trying to keep pace at speed.

quiz.question: According to Bengaluru police, what have they identified after a Ganesh idol theft from a roadside stall was caught on CCTV?
options: A single repeat offender acting alone
An organised gang targeting multiple stalls
No pattern — police called it a one-off
quiz.why: Festival-week vendors are frequent targets for opportunistic and organised theft alike, since a stall owner's attention is often split between customers and stock.

quiz.question: What's the current status of the proposed two-wheeler ban on Bengaluru's Airport Road and Electronics City flyovers?
quiz.why: Traffic restrictions like this are often piloted or reviewed before a full rollout — it's worth checking official notices rather than assuming a plan is already in effect.

quiz.question: Brent crude oil prices crossed which milestone this week as US-Iran tensions escalated?
quiz.why: Brent crude is the global benchmark price; since India imports most of its crude, a sustained rise like this tends to show up at the pump within a few weeks.

quiz.question: In India, which body sets the repo rate that indirectly affects your home and car loan EMIs?
quiz.why: A lower repo rate makes it cheaper for banks to borrow, which usually gets passed on as lower loan interest rates — and a higher one works the other way.

quiz.question: Which river, central to a long-running water-sharing dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, originates in Karnataka?
quiz.why: The Kaveri rises in Karnataka's Kodagu district and flows into Tamil Nadu, and disputes over sharing its water have run for well over a century.
